newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel hands over remains of two Hamas men.
newsitem.headline: Israel hands over remains of two Hamas men.

text.p: Israel handed over the remains of two Islamic militants to the Palestinian Authority in self-ruled Gaza on Wednesday, more than two years after the guerrillas were killed, witnesses said.

They said the bodies of Salah Jadallah and Hassan Abbas, members of the Hamas Islamic Resistance Movement, were brought in two pine coffins aboard two Israeli army trucks to the Erez checkpoint between Israel and Gaza and handed to PLO police.
The two guerrillas had been buried in a military graveyard in northern Israel since they were killed by Israeli security forces in 1994.

Members of the Abbas and Jadallah families waited on the Palestinian side of the checkpoint while PLO police officers carried the coffins one by one to ambulances. The bodies were taken to Gaza City where they were handed to the families in the presence of Hamas leaders Sayed Abu Musameh and Ahmed Bahar.

"I wish they returned the body a long time ago. The Israeli behaviour shows that Israel is a criminal state but claims democracy," said Bilal Jadallah, Salah's 20-year-old brother who is a student at Gaza's Islamic University.

Salah Jadallah was killed when Israeli troops stormed a West Bank hideout to free soldier Nachshon Waxman who Hamas had kidnapped and was holding hostage. Abbas was killed in Jerusalem during an attack on Israelis at a mall of sidewalk cafes.
Israeli media said the return of the bodies was part of a deal in which Israel last year recovered the remains of soldier Ilan Saadon who was kidnapped and killed by Hamas in 1989.
But Israeli army spokesman Oded Ben Ami denied that there was any deal.

"After the body of Ilan Saadon was found, we don't see any point any longer in keeping the bodies," Ben Ami told the radio. "There isn't and wasn't any deal between the army and anyone whatsoever in the matter of returning these bodies."
Palestinian security sources blasted Israel for holding bodies of Palestinians killed during attacks inside the Jewish state, saying that the practice amounted to holding "hostages".
"The handing over of the the bodies of Salah and Hassan does not end the practice. The Israeli government is still holding the bodies of many other Palestinians as hostages," one source said.

Israel has in the past traded bodies of guerrillas for the remains of soldiers killed in Lebanon. Guerrillas killed in clashes with Israeli forces are often buried in numbered graves at the cemetery in northern Israel.
